mainTopic: Bird and cheese: whether the table rule is a גזירה לגזירה, the משנה of בית שמאי and בית הלל, and washing hands and cleaning the mouth between cheese and meat.
overview: The amud opens by finishing רב יוסף's proof from חלת חוצה לארץ, which he used to show that חכמים do not make a גזירה לגזירה. אביי rejects the proof: outside ארץ ישראל there was nothing to decree about, but bird and cheese could lead to real meat and milk, which is Torah law. רב ששת objects that a table holds cold food with cold food, so the rule still looks like a decree on a decree. The answer is first that the worry is a boiling pot. Since a pot on the table is only a כלי שני, the answer is corrected to a כלי ראשון, which really cooks. Then a new משנה brings the מחלוקת of בית שמאי and בית הלל about bird and cheese on one table, which applies only to an eating table. The גמרא asks what רבי יוסי adds, and concludes that he is the תנא קמא, since quoting someone by name brings redemption. Next, אגרא teaches that bird and cheese may be eaten without washing hands or wiping the mouth. A story with רב יצחק shows that hand washing between cheese and meat is needed only at night. The amud ends with a ברייתא where בית שמאי say to wipe the mouth and בית הלל say to rinse it, and the גמרא asks what these words mean. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the proof from the חלה of outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's quoted משנה ends: חלה from outside ארץ ישראל may be eaten at a table with a non-כהן and given to any כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: [חלה from outside ארץ ישראל] may be eaten with a non-כהן at the same table, and may be given to any כהן one wants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote that רב יוסף began just before this line. The quote is from a משנה about חלת חוצה לארץ. He uses it to show that חכמים do not make one decree to protect another decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The obligation of חלה outside ארץ ישראל is itself only rabbinic. Even so, חכמים did not add a second decree banning a non-כהן from the table. That suggests חכמים never stack one decree on top of another.

keyTerms.meaning: חלה taken from dough outside ארץ ישראל, which is only a rabbinic obligation
A decree made to protect another decree, which חכמים generally avoid

phrases.english: It may be eaten with a non-priest at the table,
phrases.notes: "It" means חלה from outside ארץ ישראל. That subject was named just before this line.

phrases.english: and may be given to any priest that one wishes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב יוסף's citation, which started before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That חכמים do not make a גזירה לגזירה, and therefore עוף בחלב must be Torah law.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מסכת חלה about חלת חוצה לארץ.

steps.title: אביי: the proof would only work in a different case
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the proof would work only if the משנה were talking about foreign חלה brought into ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: I would agree if the משנה had taught us about חלה from outside ארץ ישראל that is now in ארץ ישראל. There, we might decree because of ארץ ישראל חלה, which is Torah law. If we still did not decree, you could learn something from it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts to reject רב יוסף's proof. First he describes the kind of case that really would have proven the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ארץ ישראל, people could mix up foreign חלה with local חלה, which is Torah law. That would be a real reason to make a second decree. Choosing not to decree in that case would show that חכמים avoid stacking decrees.

keyTerms.meaning: "It would make sense if..."; it grants one case in order to contrast it with another
חלה from ארץ ישראל, which is Torah law

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
It would be fine if it had taught us
about ḥalla from outside the Land that is in the Land,
where there is reason to decree
because of ḥalla of the Land, which is Torah law,
and yet we do not decree,
then there would be something to learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts rejecting the proof brought in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only, not necessarily רב יוסף's conclusion.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה is not a case where there was any real reason to decree.

steps.title: Why bird and cheese is different from foreign חלה
steps.stepSummary: Outside ארץ ישראל there is simply nothing to decree about. Bird and cheese, however, could lead people to eat real meat with milk, which is Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה is about חלה outside ארץ ישראל, and there they did not decree only because there was nothing to decree about. Here, if you let people put bird and cheese on the table, they will come to put meat and cheese there and eat בשר בחלב, which is Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his rejection. He explains why the חלה משנה tells us nothing about the bird-and-cheese case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With foreign חלה outside ארץ ישראל, no Torah law is anywhere nearby, so there was no reason for a decree. With bird and cheese, real animal meat and milk, a Torah prohibition, is close by. So בית הלל's decree could exist even if עוף בחלב is only rabbinic, which means רב יוסף's proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no reason to decree
To place or bring up (onto the table)
Meat cooked in milk, forbidden by Torah law

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's point: a decree only shows that חכמים "stacked" decrees if there was a real reason to decree. Outside ארץ ישראל there was none, so the חלה משנה proves nothing.

phrases.english: But it is about outside the Land,
and that is because there is nothing to decree about.
But here, if you permit him
to place bird and cheese on the table,
he will come to place meat and cheese,
and to eat meat in milk, which is Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא חוּצָה לְאָרֶץ, מִשּׁוּם דְּלֵיכָּא לְמִיגְזַר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's rejection that began in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the חלה משנה and the bird-and-cheese case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There was nothing to decree about outside ארץ ישראל, while bird and cheese sit close to a Torah prohibition.

steps.title: רב ששת: it is still cold food with cold food
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת objects that placing food on a table is cold with cold. Even real meat and milk eaten cold is not Torah law, so the table rule still looks like a decree on a decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת challenged it: In the end, it is cold food with cold food!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת raises a challenge. He says that even if עוף בחלב were Torah law, the table rule would still be a decree on top of a decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah forbids meat and milk that are cooked together. Eating cold meat with cold cheese is itself only rabbinic. So banning them from even sharing a table protects a rabbinic rule, and that is a גזירה לגזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it; it introduces a strong objection
Cold food together with cold food, which is not cooking

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב ששת is saying the food is permitted. He agrees the table rule exists. His question is that it seems to be a decree protecting another decree.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet objected to it:
Ultimately, it is cold with cold!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רב יוסף's basic idea and attacks it from a new angle.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the table decree protects a Torah law directly.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cold meat with cold milk is only rabbinic, so a decree about the table protects a rabbinic rule, which makes it a גזירה לגזירה.

steps.title: אביי: the worry is a boiling pot
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the decree is aimed at a real Torah danger: the person might put the food into a hot pot and cook it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is a decree in case he puts it into a boiling pot.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב ששת's challenge. He shows that the table decree directly protects a Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If bird and cheese are allowed on the table together, a person might put them into a boiling pot. That would be real cooking, which is Torah law if עוף בחלב is Torah law. So the decree is one step away from a Torah prohibition, and it is not a decree on a decree.

keyTerms.meaning: A decree made in case something happens

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's first answer: the table rule protects against Torah-level cooking in a boiling pot. The next step challenges this, and step 7 corrects it to a כלי ראשון.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is a decree lest he place it
in a boiling pot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יַעֲלֶה בְּאִילְפָּס רוֹתֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's challenge from step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes what the decree is protecting against
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The table decree protects against eating cold with cold, which is only rabbinic.
steps.terutzMaskana: The table decree protects against cooking in a boiling pot, which is Torah law.

steps.title: But a pot on the table is only a secondary vessel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to אביי: any pot on the table is a כלי שני, and a כלי שני does not cook.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, it is a secondary vessel, and a secondary vessel does not cook!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's answer from step 5. A pot sitting on the table is no longer on the fire, so putting food into it is not real cooking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the decree exists because a person might put the food into a hot pot and cook it. But a pot that has been taken off the fire is a כלי שני, and a כלי שני cannot cook. So the Torah-level danger seems to disappear again, and we are back to a decree on a decree.

keyTerms.meaning: A secondary vessel: a pot the food was moved into, which was not itself on the fire

steps.confusionAlert: Being hot is not enough for a pot to 'cook' halachically. What matters is whether this is the vessel that was on the fire (כלי ראשון) or a vessel the food was moved into (כלי שני).

phrases.english: Ultimately, it is a secondary vessel,
phrases.notes: He means the hot pot from אביי's answer. Once it is on the table, it is no longer the vessel that was on the fire.

phrases.english: and a secondary vessel does not cook!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's answer in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the table decree guards against cooking in a hot pot.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A pot on the table is a כלי שני, and a כלי שני does not cook. So no Torah prohibition could result, and the decree again looks like a decree on a decree.

steps.title: The decree is about a primary pot
steps.stepSummary: The decree really guards against putting the food into a כלי ראשון, which does cook.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a decree lest he put it into a primary pot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the answer. The worry is that the person will put the meat and cheese into a pot that was actually on the fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלי ראשון does cook. Meat and milk cooked together that way is a real Torah prohibition. So the table rule is a single decree protecting against a Torah violation, not a decree on a decree.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (a correction of the previous idea)
A rabbinic decree made to keep people away from a real prohibition
A primary pot: the one that was itself on the fire

steps.whatToRemember: The table rule is a single rabbinic decree. It exists because eating at the same table might lead to putting the food into a כלי ראשון, which would be real Torah-level cooking of meat and milk.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a decree
lest he put it into a primary pot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יַעֲלֶה בְּאִילְפָּס רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 6 by moving the concern to a כלי ראשון.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree was about a hot pot on the table, which is only a כלי שני and does not cook.
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree is about a כלי ראשון, which does cook, so the danger is a real Torah prohibition.

steps.title: משנה: bird meat and cheese on one table
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי allow bird meat and cheese on the same table but not eating them together. בית הלל forbid both. רבי יוסי says this is a case where בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bird meat may be put on the table together with cheese, but it is not eaten with it. These are the words of בית שמאי. בית הלל say: it is neither put on the table nor eaten. רבי יוסי said: this is one of the leniencies of בית שמאי and the stringencies of בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It records a dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל about bird meat and cheese sharing a table.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that bird meat and cheese are not eaten together. The argument is only about putting them on the same table: בית שמאי allow it and בית הלל forbid it. רבי יוסי adds that this is one of the rare cases where בית שמאי are the lenient side.

keyTerms.meaning: Is put up on the table

keyTerms.term: קוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וְחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל
keyTerms.meaning: Cases where בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict

steps.confusionAlert: Usually בית שמאי are the strict side. Here it is the other way around, and that is exactly why רבי יוסי points it out.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Bird meat may go up together with cheese
onto the table, but it is not eaten with it,
these are the words of בית שמאי.
And בית הלל say:
it neither goes up onto the table nor is eaten.
רבי יוסי said:
This is one of the leniencies of בית שמאי
and the stringencies of בית הלל.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָעוֹף עוֹלֶה עִם הַגְּבִינָה עַל הַשּׁוּלְחָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the earlier discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: bird meat and cheese may share a table but are not eaten together. בית הלל: they may not even share a table. רבי יוסי: this is a leniency of בית שמאי and a stringency of בית הלל.

steps.title: Which table the rule applies to
steps.stepSummary: The rule applies only to a table one eats at. On a table used for setting out food, meat and cheese may be placed side by side.
steps.simpleTranslation: About which table did they say this? About a table one eats at. But on a table where one sets out the cooked food, he may put this next to that and need not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה narrows its own rule. It tells us which kind of table the ban is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is about mixing while eating. So it only applies to the table where people actually eat. A table used just to arrange or serve food carries no such risk, so meat and cheese may sit side by side there.
steps.whatToRemember: The ban on meat and cheese sharing a table applies only to the eating table, not to a table used for setting out food.

phrases.english: About which table did they say this?
About a table that one eats at,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּשׁוּלְחָן שֶׁסּוֹדֵר עָלָיו אֶת הַתַּבְשִׁיל –
phrases.english: but on a table where one sets out the cooked food,
one may put this next to that,
phrases.notes: This means the meat next to the cheese.

phrases.english: and need not worry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the 'table' in the rule of step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The table rule applies only to an eating table. On a serving or preparation table, meat and cheese may be placed side by side.

steps.title: Isn't רבי יוסי saying the same as the תנא קמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יוסי adds, since the תנא קמא already showed בית שמאי as lenient and בית הלל as strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: Isn't רבי יוסי the same as the תנא קמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by questioning רבי יוסי's statement in the משנה. It seems to add nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the משנה already shows בית שמאי allowing the table and בית הלל forbidding it. Calling this 'a leniency of בית שמאי' seems to just repeat that. A משנה should not record an opinion that changes nothing, so the גמרא asks what the difference is.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
The first, unnamed teacher of the משנה

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא?
phrases.english: GEMARA: Isn't רבי יוסי the same as the first tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's statement in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His statement seems to repeat what the תנא קמא already said, so it should not need to be recorded.

steps.title: Suggestion: they differ about eating itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the תנא קמא limits the dispute to the table, while רבי יוסי says בית שמאי and בית הלל argue even about eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that eating itself is the difference between them: the תנא קמא says they argue only about placing on the table and do not argue about eating. And רבי יוסי said to him: eating itself is one of the leniencies of בית שמאי and the stringencies of בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to its own question. It proposes that רבי יוסי and the תנא קמא disagree about whether בית שמאי allow eating bird meat with cheese.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the תנא קמא, both houses forbid eating, and the argument is only about the table. By this suggestion, רבי יוסי holds that בית שמאי even allow eating, which is a much bigger leniency. The opening 'וכי תימא' signals that the גמרא is about to show this idea does not hold up.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: introduces a suggested answer the גמרא will test
There is a difference between them
Putting the food up onto the table

steps.confusionAlert: This is only a suggestion. 'וכי תימא' means the גמרא is setting up an idea in order to knock it down, so it is not the final answer.

phrases.english: And if you would say:
eating itself is the difference between them,
since the first tanna says:
they argue about putting it on the table,
but about eating they do not argue,
and רבי יוסי said to him:
eating itself is one of the leniencies of בית שמאי
and the stringencies of בית הלל.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: אֲכִילָה גּוּפַהּ אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the question of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Suggested difference between opinions (tentative, about to be tested)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי seems to repeat the תנא קמא exactly.
steps.terutzMaskana: Suggestion: the תנא קמא limits the dispute to the table, while רבי יוסי extends בית שמאי's leniency to eating itself.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that even בית שמאי forbid eating bird with cheese
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quoting רבי יוסי shows that בית שמאי also forbid eating bird with cheese, so there is no argument about eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches that רבי יוסי says: there are six cases where בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict, and this is one of them. Bird may be put on the table with cheese but not eaten with it, says בית שמאי. בית הלל say it may not be put there and may not be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer from step 11. A ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי himself says בית שמאי forbid eating bird with cheese.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 suggested that, according to רבי יוסי, בית שמאי and בית הלל argue even about eating. But in this ברייתא רבי יוסי says plainly that בית שמאי agree it is 'not eaten', so both sides forbid eating. The only argument is about putting the two foods on the same table, and the suggested answer falls.

keyTerms.meaning: Leniencies; cases where someone rules the easier way
Stringencies; cases where someone rules the stricter way
Literally 'goes up on the table'; is placed on the same table

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Yosei says:
Six matters are among the leniencies of Beit Shammai
and the stringencies of Beit Hillel,
and this is one of them:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹף עוֹלֶה עִם הַגְּבִינָה עַל הַשּׁוּלְחָן,
phrases.english: Bird meat may be placed with cheese on the table,
but it is not eaten with it; these are the words of Beit Shammai.
And Beit Hillel say:
It is neither placed there nor eaten!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer suggested in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that, according to רבי יוסי, בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about eating too.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוסי's own ברייתא says בית שמאי forbid eating, so there is no argument about eating.

steps.title: The new point is that the first opinion is really רבי יוסי's
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי's words come to tell us that the unnamed first opinion in the משנה is his.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what it teaches us: who is the תנא קמא? It is רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the question of step 10. רבי יוסי's statement does not add a new law. It tells us who said the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law is the same in both parts: בית שמאי are lenient about the table and בית הלל are strict. What רבי יוסי's words add is the name of the person behind the unnamed first opinion, which is רבי יוסי himself.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it comes to teach us
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it teaches us:
Who is the first tanna? Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 12 rejected the earlier answer, this gives a new answer to step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying who said an opinion: the words tell us who said it, not a new law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יוסי must be adding a new law, such as an argument about eating.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי adds no new law. He tells us that the first opinion is his.

steps.title: Quoting someone by name brings redemption
steps.stepSummary: Saying a teaching in the name of the person who said it brings redemption, as we learn from אסתר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever says something in the name of the person who said it brings redemption to the world, as it says: 'And אסתר told the king in the name of מרדכי.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why it matters to know that the first opinion is רבי יוסי's. Giving credit to the person who said something is very important.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing the name might seem like a small detail, but it has real value. אסתר told the king about the plot in מרדכי's name, and this led to the redemption of פורים.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of the one who said it

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known lesson about giving proper credit when you repeat what you learned.

phrases.english: Whoever says a thing in the name of the one who said it
brings redemption to the world,
as it is said: "And Esther told the king in the name of Mordechai."

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר דָּבָר בְּשֵׁם אוֹמְרוֹ מֵבִיא גְּאוּלָּה לָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the answer in step 13 is worth teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying a teaching in the name of the person who said it brings redemption.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's statement adds no new law. It tells us that the first opinion is his, and giving proper credit is very valuable.

steps.title: אגרא teaches that bird and cheese may be eaten freely
steps.stepSummary: אגרא, the father-in-law of רבי אבא, teaches that bird and cheese may be eaten one after the other without worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: אגרא, the father-in-law of רבי אבא, taught: bird and cheese may be eaten freely.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. אגרא teaches that one can be relaxed about eating bird and cheese one after the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אגרא says no special care is needed when eating bird and cheese one after the other. The exact meaning of 'freely' is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Freely, without worry or special care

phrases.english: Agra, the father-in-law of Rabbi Abba, taught:
Bird and cheese may be eaten freely.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about bird and cheese.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bird and cheese may be eaten without special care.

steps.title: אגרא explains what 'freely' means
steps.stepSummary: אגרא explains that 'freely' means without washing hands and without wiping the mouth between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught it, and he explained it: without washing hands and without wiping the mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The same teacher who said the rule now explains it. 'Freely' means you do not need to wash your hands or clean your mouth between eating bird and cheese.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually one washes the hands and cleans the mouth between eating meat and cheese. For bird and cheese, אגרא says neither one is needed.

keyTerms.term: הוּא תָנֵי לַהּ וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ
keyTerms.meaning: He taught it and he himself explained it

phrases.aramaic: הוּא תָנֵי לַהּ, וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ:
phrases.english: He taught it, and he explained it:

phrases.aramaic: בְּלֹא נְטִילַת יָדַיִם וּבְלֹא קִינּוּחַ הַפֶּה.
phrases.english: without washing the hands and without wiping the mouth.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא תָנֵי לַהּ, וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the word בְּאַפִּיקוֹרַן from step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Between bird and cheese, no hand washing and no mouth wiping are needed.

steps.title: רב יצחק eats cheese and then meat without washing his hands
steps.stepSummary: At רב אשי's house, רב יצחק בריה דרב משרשיא ate cheese and then meat without washing his hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק, son of רב משרשיא, came to רב אשי's house. They brought him cheese and he ate it. They brought him meat and he ate it, and he did not wash his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. It sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This was animal meat, not bird meat. So his behavior seems to go beyond אגרא's rule, which spoke only about bird.

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak, son of Rav Mesharshiya,
happened to come to the house of Rav Ashi.
They brought him cheese, and he ate it.
They brought him meat, and he ate it,
and he did not wash his hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells a story that tests אגרא's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sage ate cheese and then animal meat without washing his hands in between.

steps.title: The household challenges him from אגרא's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The people in רב אשי's house argue that אגרא allowed this only for bird and cheese, not for meat and cheese.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But אגרא, the father-in-law of רבי אבא, taught that bird and cheese may be eaten freely. Bird and cheese, yes. Meat and cheese, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The people at רב אשי's house challenge רב יצחק's behavior. They point out that אגרא's teaching mentioned only bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They learn from what אגרא did not say. Since אגרא named only bird and cheese, they conclude that animal meat and cheese still need hand washing in between. So רב יצחק seems to have acted against אגרא's teaching.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the challenge is about eating meat and cheese together. He ate them one after the other. The question is only whether he needed to wash his hands in between.

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא תָּאנֵי אַגְרָא חֲמוּהּ דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא:
phrases.english: But didn't Agra, the father-in-law of Rabbi Abba, teach:
Bird and cheese may be eaten freely.
Bird and cheese, yes;
meat and cheese, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: וְהָא תָּאנֵי אַגְרָא חֲמוּהּ דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what רב יצחק did in step 17, using אגרא's teaching from steps 15 and 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יצחק בריה דרב משרשיא eating animal meat after cheese without washing his hands.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since אגרא allowed this only for bird and cheese, animal meat and cheese must still need washing in between.

steps.title: Washing is only needed at night, when you cannot see
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק answers the challenge: hand washing between cheese and meat is needed only at night. By day he can see that his hands are clean.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: That rule applies at night. But by day, I can see.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק defends what he did. He explains that the need to wash hands between cheese and meat is only at night, and he ate during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason to wash hands is that bits of cheese might still be on them. At night you cannot check, so you must wash. In daylight you can look and see that your hands are clean, so washing is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: These words, meaning 'this rule applies only to...'
I see, I can look and check

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the hand washing has a practical reason: it is about food that might be left on the hands, so seeing clearly can make it unnecessary.

phrases.english: He said to them:
phrases.notes: This is רב יצחק answering the people in רב אשי's house.

phrases.english: This applies only at night,
phrases.notes: He means washing hands between cheese and meat is needed only at night.

phrases.english: but by day, I can see.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 18 against רב יצחק's behavior in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule: washing is needed only when you cannot check, which is at night.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The household assumed one must always wash hands between cheese and meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: Washing is needed only at night. By day you can see your hands are clean, so you need not wash.

steps.title: בית שמאי say wipe, בית הלל say rinse
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a מחלוקת: בית שמאי require wiping the mouth, and בית הלל require rinsing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: בית שמאי say one wipes, and בית הלל say one rinses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on cleaning the mouth between eating dairy and meat. בית שמאי say you wipe it and בית הלל say you rinse it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 already spoke about wiping the mouth. Now we learn there is a מחלוקת about which kind of cleaning is required. The two words are not yet explained, and the גמרא will ask about them next.

phrases.english: It was taught: Beit Shammai say: One wipes,
phrases.notes: This means cleaning the mouth between cheese and meat.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: One rinses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from hand washing to a ברייתא about cleaning the mouth, connected to the wiping in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: one wipes the mouth. בית הלל: one rinses the mouth.

steps.title: What do 'wipe' and 'rinse' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly מקנח and מדיח mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'wipes,' and what is 'rinses'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the two words in the ברייתא. This is a setup question, and the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave two words without explaining them. Before we can understand the מחלוקת, we need to know what each one involves.

phrases.english: What is 'wipes,'
and what is 'rinses'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the terms in the ברייתא from step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact meaning of מקנח and מדיח in the ברייתא.
